newsitem.title: USA: Chevron to expand paraxylene capacity.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to expand paraxylene capacity.

text.p: Chevron Corp will spend $200 million to double the capacity of existing paraxylene manufacturing facilities at its Pascagoula refinery, General Manager Graham Somerville said Monday.

Chevron Chemical Co foresees the worldwide paraxylene market growing worldwide more than seven percent annually for the remainder of the decade, said John Gaston, Fiber Intermediates General Manager, U.S. Chemicals Division.
Chevron has been a producer and seller of paraxylene, an aromatic petrochemical derived from benzene, since the beginnings of the polyester market in the 1950s, he noted.
"Fiber consumption is growing with the economies of the Pacific Rim, as is consumer demand in the U.S. for the convenience of paraxylene-based plastic bottles and containers," Gaston observed.

The refinery's current annual production capacity for paraxylene -- a petrochemical feedstock used in the manufacture of polyester fibers, plastic bottles and film -- is 500 million pounds. When the expansion is completed, capacity will total slightly over one billion pounds per year.
Construction of the paraxylene expansion is slated to begin as early as the fourth quarter of this year.
Somerville said the required environmental permit applications were submitted to the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality in May, and all approvals are anticipated within a month.

He said the proposed paraxylene expansion will use a proprietary manufacturing technology, called Eluxyl, which was jointly developed by Chevron and Institut Francais Du Petrole. "A year-long pilot project was conducted at the refinery to test the Eluxyl process, and the test results were very positive," he said.
Somerville said Bechtel Corp will perform engineering, procurement and construction for the paraxylene expansion.
Chevron's Pascagoula Refinery began operations in 1963, and today processes an average 295,000 barrels of crude oil daily. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
